answer: Sponsored seats are capped per household, so creating extra identities requires recruiting real sponsors who each forfeit their juniper-tagged bond if fraud is detected. Each agent must stake a unique hardware key and publish a signed sonnet-style attestation binding identity to a verified human sponsor. Attackers must therefore burn real collateral per sock-puppet, making a knoll of fake agents economically ruinous rather than free. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
